title: Authentication, sessions and company accounts
summary: Atomic current account journeys, local-only password boundaries and managed identity candidates. Source-backed implementation status is not a runtime verification result. Existing test paths are related references, not claims of complete per-case coverage.

expected: The sign-in route includes the requested local URL as returnTo.

cases.title: Discard superseded successful login
preconditions: No application session is installed; local cases use explicit loopback development unless the scenario describes the managed provider.
steps: Begin one login and replace the session before its successful reply arrives.
expected: The older result returns superseded and cannot install the old account.
notes: This is an internal frontend AuthService epoch invariant. The current public sign-in form disables another submit while busy; it is not a browser journey. Real Go responses can be delayed without fabricating data in a typed Injector/LocalSignIn Playwright Node integration. Browser duplicate-submit protection is separately UC-ACC-0012.

cases.title: Sign in with an approved provisioned hosted-password account
preconditions: The isolated service uses production VM password mode with its own provisioned credentials, a canonical HTTPS application origin and PostgreSQL verify-full TLS.
steps: Submit the provisioned username and exact password from the hosted password screen and through the password HTTP operation.
expected: A short-lived REST token is installed only after current company approval is verified; the web app opens the approved account.
notes: Local integration exercises the actual password mode. It does not establish a deployed VM, public TLS certificate or cloud-provider acceptance.

cases.title: Reject a hosted REST token used directly as an MCP credential

The approved account has a newly issued hosted password REST token.
steps: Read the REST identity with that token, then submit the same token directly to MCP.
expected: The REST identity succeeds and the MCP boundary rejects the mismatched audience.
notes: Local integration exercises the actual password mode. It does not establish a deployed VM, public TLS certificate or cloud-provider acceptance.

cases.title: Keep delayed previous-session project replies from canceling a replacement login
preconditions: An approved owner has an accepted project read whose response is delayed in the browser.
A different approved member is signing in on the same page after sign-out.
steps: Sign out and begin the member login while its successful credential response is delayed.
Deliver the previous owner project response, then deliver the member credential response.
expected: The obsolete project response starts no unsigned board discovery and cannot invalidate the pending login.
The replacement member identity and board directory load with authenticated requests and the correct project role, without a document reload.
notes: The browser story delays actual accepted service responses; it does not replace identity or project service responses with invented fixtures.
